fields.description:
## Symptom

`make worktree name=<branch>` fails immediately for every invocation:

```
/bin/sh: branch: No such file or directory
make: *** [worktree] Error 1
```

No worktree is created. The documented one-command path for provisioning a worktree is
therefore unusable, and `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` both direct agents and
contributors to it.

## Root cause

In the `worktree` target the recipe line

```
	@set -e; \
```

ends with a backslash continuation, but the line that follows it is an `@#`-prefixed
comment:

```
	@set -e; \
	@# Default is ~/worktrees/rebar/<branch>, NOT a sibling of the checkout.
```

Make strips a recipe line's `@` prefix and treats `#` as a comment only at the start of
a recipe line. Here the previous line continues into this one, so make joins them and
hands the shell a single command:

```
set -e; @# Default is ~/worktrees/rebar/<branch>, NOT a sibling of the checkout.
```

`#` does not begin a shell comment mid-word, so the shell parses that text as a command
and reads `<branch>` as an **input redirection** from a file named `branch`. No such
file exists, producing `/bin/sh: branch: No such file or directory`.

## The second defect behind the first

Fixing only the parse error would leave a subtler regression in place, so the remedy has
to address both together.

The `set -e` was deliberately introduced to fix bug 1738: make applies no `set -e`
semantics *inside* a recipe line, checking only the line's overall status, which is its
last command's. Without it a failed `make venv` or `make install` was discarded and the
target printed "✓ worktree ready" and exited 0, handing back a worktree with no usable
`.venv`. The recipe's own comment block documents exactly this.

But because the comment block terminates the continued line, `set -e` is now stranded on
a line of its own, and the entire body — `target_dir=`, the fetch, the `git worktree
add`, and the venv provisioning — begins a *new* recipe line that `set -e` never governs.
So bug 1738's protection is already detached. A fix that merely relocates the comments
without rejoining `set -e` to the body would restore the target to working order while
silently leaving it able to report success over a failed provisioning step again.

## The default directory is unwritable, and has been twice

The default is `$HOME/worktrees/rebar/<branch>`. Ticket `9b4a-89fb-3328-497e` moved it
there from a sibling of the checkout, because a sibling resolves to the home directory
for a clone at `~/rebar`, which the agent filesystem sandbox refuses to write.

That fix substituted one unwritable location for another: `$HOME/worktrees/` is outside
the sandbox boundary as well. The default has therefore never worked under the sandbox,
and the failure still surfaces as a broken `git worktree add` rather than as a denial,
which is exactly the misreading `9b4a` set out to prevent.

Three conventions are currently in circulation and no two agree:

- `AGENTS.md` line 441 documents `git worktree add ../<name>` — a sibling, unwritable.
- The `worktree` target defaults to `$HOME/worktrees/rebar/<name>` — unwritable.
- Every worktree that actually exists lives under `.rebar/worktrees/<name>`, which is
  inside the sandbox and is covered by the `.rebar/*` entry in `.gitignore`, so nested
  worktrees never appear as untracked files in the outer checkout. `git worktree list`
  currently shows 12 of them there and none at either documented location.

The remedy adopts the convention that demonstrably works and makes the two documented
ones agree with it.

## Remedy

1. Relocate the explanatory comment block so it sits above `set -e` as a standalone
   recipe comment rather than inside a continued line, preserving its content.
2. Rejoin `set -e` to the body so it governs every step, restoring bug 1738's
   protection rather than merely un-breaking the parse.
3. Change the default target directory to `.rebar/worktrees/<name>` within the
   checkout. `dir=` continues to override.
4. Update `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` so the documented manual path matches the
   target's default instead of naming a sibling directory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `make worktree name=<branch>` with no `dir=` creates a worktree at
      `.rebar/worktrees/<branch>` branched from a freshly-fetched `origin/main` and
      provisions a working `.venv`, verified by running it and showing the resulting
      `git worktree list` entry and a `.venv/bin/python` that executes.
- [ ] `make worktree name=<branch> dir=<path>` still honours the explicit path,
      verified the same way.
- [ ] A provisioning failure makes the target exit non-zero rather than printing
      "✓ worktree ready", verified by forcing the provisioning step to fail and showing
      the exit status. This is bug 1738's invariant and it must be demonstrated, not
      assumed from the presence of `set -e`.
- [ ] A test asserts the `worktree` recipe expands to syntactically valid shell, by
      taking `make -n worktree name=<x>` and feeding the expansion to `sh -n`. This
      catches the whole class of recipe-quoting and continuation defects rather than the
      single `@#` token, and it depends on no CI provider. The test fails against the
      current Makefile before the fix.
- [ ] The explanatory comments are preserved and are real make comments rather than
      shell text, verified by the diff.
- [ ] `make worktree` with no `name=` still prints its usage message and exits 2,
      verified by the command's output and exit status, and the usage text names the new
      default.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` no longer direct readers to a worktree path that
      the sandbox refuses to write, verified by the diff.
- [ ] Nothing the target creates by default appears as untracked in `git status`,
      verified by running it and showing clean output.
